notes: Hermes maintains a single-session task list via the `todo` tool (tools/todo_tool.py: full-list replace by default, items {id, content, status}, statuses pending|in_progress|completed|cancelled, one in_progress at a time). The driver asks hermes to create three items and walk each pending -> in_progress -> completed in one `hermes chat` session, with no delegate_task, so SubagentCount stays 0. The lifecycle arc (ready -> working -> ready) IS observable today: finish_reason='stop' on the newest assistant row is an explicit turn boundary (parser.go:93, watcher.go turnIsDone), and the open todo tool calls hold the session in working in between. Birth is modelled in TWO phases because hermes declares a ProcessMatcher: processlifecycle mints a transient proc-<PID> presession at launch while the real sessions row (id shaped YYYYMMDD_HHMMSS_<hex6>) is INSERTed ~2s later on the first user message. KNOWN FAILING: the load-bearing task-content observable is NOT produced. The store persists the todo call verbatim - the assistant row's tool_calls column carries function.arguments with the todos[] snapshot, and the paired role='tool' row carries todo_tool's full-list return payload - but core/adapters/inbound/agents/hermes/parser.go's parseToolCalls (lines 118-145) unmarshals only {id, call_id, function.name} and drops function.arguments, and metrics.go's querySessionMetrics never assigns metrics.Tasks or metrics.AppliedTaskDeltas. So the session API tasks field stays empty and SessionDetector.recordTaskDeltas (session_detector_activity.go:746) records ZERO task_delta events. That is a parser/metrics gap, not architectural incapability: the same full-list-snapshot signal on the same ProcessOwnedStore transport is already handled for opencode (parser.go:276 appendTodowriteDeltas + metrics.go:159), and hermes' todo items carry a stable id so the reconciliation is id-keyed rather than content-keyed. The task_tracked phase below asserts the CORRECT behaviour and is the phase this cell pins; note that a fix mirroring opencode exactly (Tasks only, no AppliedTaskDeltas) would satisfy the API field but leave this phase red - the intended fix populates both (#662). Observations deliberately pin neither model nor cost: the recording home's model is a human choice, and irrlicht prices hermes from its own alias table, which has no entry for the locally configured gpt-5.6-luna (EstimateCostUSD returns 0 for an unpriced model, capacity.go:159-162) while Hermes itself reports estimated_cost_usd=0.0 under subscription billing. tokens_nonzero is safe - the sessions row carries input/output aggregates.
